The court also reversed a later trial-court order that had sent the appeals concerning the cease-and-desist orders back to the administrative board. It said the proper route was to remand the penalty appeal so that technical-assistance evidence that had been wrongly excluded could be considered. That ruling did not resolve the entire dispute over the penalties. The case subsequently moved to the Washington Supreme Court, which agreed to review the matter in June 2026. The Pacific Legal Foundation says the Supreme Court case concerns whether the Department of Ecology must comply with the legislature’s limits on its enforcement authority. The organisation is representing Fodé without charge. The Supreme Court heard arguments on October 1.The prolonged dispute has had a substantial effect on the family’s agricultural operation. The Fodés said they have had to sell nearly everything they once farmed, reducing their operation from 4,000 acres of owned and leased land to 290 leased acres. They argue that the conflict could have been avoided if the agency had helped them identify a lawful route to irrigation before imposing penalties. The court’s decision will determine the legal questions before it. Until then, the dispute remains unresolved, and the Fodés continue to challenge the state’s handling of their irrigation application and the penalties that followed.
Article Summary: Ron Fodé and his wife, Robin, say the agency refused to help them find a lawful way to irrigate their crops before imposing penalties. The case has reached the Washington Supreme Court, which heard arguments on October 1, 2026. At its centre is a question about whether the state agency followed a law requiring it to provide technical assistance to water users before moving to penalties.

Article Title: A pig became famous after running through Hollywood; Oscar-nominated songwriter Diane Warren won him in a silent auction and sent him to a 7-acre sanctuary
Article Text:
PC: ABC News

Wilbur the pig attracts four hopeful adopters after his West Hollywood rescue

Diane Warren wins bid to give Wilbur a new home at her Malibu sanctuary

A seven-acre sanctuary in Malibu

Warren jokes about her Oscar record

Wilbur the pig went from wandering through a West Hollywood neighbourhood to becoming the unlikely focus of an adoption contest. After his appearance was captured on video and spread online, the pig was taken to the West L.A. Animal Shelter, where no owner came forward. Four people eventually expressed interest in adopting him, prompting a silent auction. As reported by ABC news, the winning bid came from Marcia Zwilling, managing director of the Diane Warren Foundation, on behalf of Oscar-nominated songwriter Diane Warren. Warren had seen footage of Wilbur and wanted him somewhere safe. He will now move to her seven-acre Malibu sanctuary, joining other rescued animals.Wilbur was first noticed wandering through a West Hollywood neighbourhood, where his unexpected appearance was captured on video. The footage circulated widely, turning the loose pig into a familiar sight to people following the story.His journey changed when he was safely taken to the West L.A. Animal Shelter. Staff waited for an owner to claim him, but nobody came forward. That left the shelter facing a rather unusual adoption situation as word about the pig continued to spread.By Thursday, four people had arrived with hopes of adopting Wilbur. With more than one prospective home interested, the shelter used a silent auction to decide who would take responsibility for him.The successful bid was made by Marcia Zwilling, managing director of the Diane Warren Foundation. She was acting on behalf of Warren, the songwriter behind numerous film songs and a 17-time Oscar nominee. According to Zwilling, Warren had seen news footage of Wilbur running through West Hollywood and immediately wanted to help. She contacted Zwilling with a simple request."Diane saw the news clips and saw the little pig running in West Hollywood and she just called me and said, 'Please get the pig, get the pig!"For Wilbur, that meant a move from the animal shelter to a very different setting. He is now headed for Warren’s seven-acre sanctuary in Malibu, where he will live alongside other rescued animals.The sanctuary is intended to give Wilbur plenty of space and company. Zwilling said he will have other animal companions around him and will be fed what she described as gourmet salads. There is also a small complication with his name. Warren already has another pig called Wilbur at the sanctuary, meaning the new arrival may eventually be given a different one.Warren has suggested “Hollywood” as a possible replacement, a fitting reference to the place where the pig first became known.Warren has spent much of her career writing songs for films and has received 17 Oscar nominations without winning the Academy Award. Her reaction to Wilbur’s arrival was characteristically light-hearted. “I lose Oscars but I won a pig,” Warren said.The remark came as Wilbur’s unusual journey reached its final stage. What began with a pig appearing unexpectedly on West Hollywood streets ended with him being claimed through an auction and given a permanent home at a private animal sanctuary.
Article Summary: Diane Warren wins bid to give Wilbur a new home at her Malibu sanctuary. The winning bid came from Marcia Zwilling, managing director of the Diane Warren Foundation. She was acting on behalf of Warren, the songwriter behind numerous film songs and a 17-time Oscar nominee.

Article Title: Hurricane Isaias kills 4 in US, leaves hundreds of thousands without power - video
Article Text:
The storm damaged buildings, uprooted trees and raised fears of flash floods and tornadoes.

Trees fall on homes, buildings damaged

Emergency declarations, flood warnings

Four people have died and hundreds of thousands have been left without electricity after Hurricane Isaias battered parts of the southern United States with powerful winds and heavy rain. The storm damaged buildings, uprooted trees and raised fears of flash floods and tornadoes across the Southeast.Officials reported two deaths each in Florida and Alabama. An estimated 500,000 people across several states were without power by Saturday evening, according to outage tracker PowerOutage.Nearly 900,000 customers had lost electricity in the initial hours after the storm made landfall, according to BBC reports.Isaias struck Florida’s Gulf Coast late Friday with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (168 km/h) before weakening into a post-tropical cyclone. Although the storm weakened overnight, officials warned that heavy rain and flooding remained a threat.In Florida’s Escambia County, a woman was killed when a tree fell on her home, while a man died from carbon monoxide poisoning after a generator was operated in his garage, Sheriff Chip Simmons said.Four members of the man’s family, aged between four and 72, were treated and were expected to survive, the Associated Press reported.In Alabama, one person died when a tree fell on a house in Birmingham, Fire Chief Cory Moon said. A second storm-related death was reported in Barbour County after a motor vehicle crash involving a fallen tree, according to Josh Johnson of the state’s emergency management agency.The storm also caused scattered damage along Florida’s Gulf Coast. Hurricane-force winds blew the roof off a hotel in Pensacola, while the city’s mayor said the airport “took some damage”. In Destin, a boathouse was flattened, and part of a high-rise building’s facade was torn away in Panama City Beach.Isaias also ripped rooftops and facades from hotels and condominiums along the Florida Panhandle. Authorities in Mobile, Alabama, reported numerous fallen trees and power lines.Alabama, Florida and Georgia declared states of emergency ahead of the storm, while Florida and Alabama issued mandatory evacuation orders for thousands of residents.US President Donald Trump approved an emergency declaration for Georgia after earlier approving similar measures for Florida and Alabama, allowing federal assistance to be provided.The US Department of Energy also authorised emergency exchanges of crude oil from the nation’s Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address potential supply disruptions caused by the storm.The National Weather Service warned that parts of Georgia and the Carolinas could experience heavy rainfall capable of triggering flash floods.Isaias was expected to move into the Tennessee Valley before reaching the mid-Atlantic region on Sunday. Forecasters also warned that flooding could extend into the Appalachian region.Despite warnings of storm surges, several major coastal routes were open by daybreak on Saturday and had avoided the widespread damage to trees and power lines often seen after major hurricanes.Meanwhile, in the Pacific Ocean, Hurricane Simon strengthened into a Category 4 storm as it approached Mexico’s coast. It was expected to bring heavy rainfall from Sunday to parts of southwestern Mexico, raising the risk of life-threatening flooding and mudslides.Tropical Storm Rachel was also forecast to bring strong winds and heavy rain to northern Mexico and Southern California over the weekend.
Article Summary: Officials reported two deaths each in Florida and Alabama. An estimated 500,000 people across several states were without power by Saturday evening. Hurricane- force winds blew the roof off a hotel in Pensacola, while the city’s mayor said the airport ‘took some damage’

Article Title: Baltimore turned waste glass into road surfaces on at least 17 streets; the crushed glass made the pavement sparkle under sunlight and streetlights
Article Text:
PC: AI Generated

How did Baltimore’s recycled glass roads create a sparkling effect

PC: AI Generated

How is crushed glass turned into a paving material

Crushed glass can affect the strength and performance of asphalt

What makes recycled glass suitable for asphalt paving

At least 17 streets in Baltimore were paved with recycled glass, creating road surfaces that could sparkle when sunlight or streetlights hit them. Baltimore's approach is part of a broader practice of using crushed waste glass in asphalt mixes. Properly processed glass can replace some of the conventional aggregate used in road construction.Wearing surfaces containing 10 to 15% crushed glass have performed well. According to the Federal Highway Administration, recycled glass has also been used in road projects elsewhere in the United States. New York City used about 225,000 metric tonnes of glass in resurfacing applications between 1990 and 1995.However, earlier projects found problems when glass was used in high percentages or as large pieces. The guidance recommends using properly processed glass in suitable proportions for asphalt paving.Waste glass was tested for use in hot mix asphalt during field demonstrations in the United States in the late 1960s and early 1970s. Test paving strips were placed at about 33 locations across the United States and Canada. Baltimore later used glass in at least 17 streets, producing a sparkle effect from reflected sunlight or street lamp light.Early projects often used more than 25% glass and coarse particles. The guidance says high glass percentages and large particles probably contributed to stripping and raveling problems reported during those demonstrations. Glass does not absorb asphalt cement binder and bonds poorly to it. Moisture damage can become a concern when high percentages and large gradations are used in surface mixes.According to the FHWA guidance, turning waste glass into a suitable paving material requires several processing steps before it can be mixed into the asphalt. Waste glass is first cleaned to remove materials such as metal, plastic, and paper. It is then crushed and screened to produce smaller, more suitable pieces while removing flat, elongated, and sharp-edged particles.For surface pavements, the guidance recommends using glass smaller than 4.75 mm, or the No. 4 sieve, as a fine aggregate mixed with conventional materials. Asphalt wearing surfaces containing 10 to 15% crushed glass have shown satisfactory performance. Higher proportions, potentially up to 25%, may be suitable for base or binder courses, where the glass is not exposed directly at the road surface.Well-crushed glass can also affect the performance of asphalt mixes because of its angular shape and high friction angle. The guidance says these properties can contribute to good lateral stability, with tests reporting stability comparable to, and in many cases better than, conventional mixes. Waste glass also has a specific gravity about 10 to 15% below that of conventional aggregates, which can increase the yield of an asphalt mix.Its low thermal conductivity may also help mixes containing glass retain heat for longer. Skid resistance tests on pavements containing waste glass have produced results within recommended limits. However, larger glass particles measuring more than 19 mm can become slippery when wet and should not be used in surface mixes. The guidance also notes that using more than 15% glass can increase pavement reflectivity and glare, particularly when the surface is wet.Asphalt mixes containing crushed glass can be designed using standard laboratory procedures. The guidance recommends testing the mix for stripping potential and says conventional pavement structural design methods are appropriate.Most highway departments allow 5 to 10% glass. The guidance says performance is generally best when crushed glass is used as a sand or fine aggregate substitute.The same methods and equipment can be used to store, mix, place, and compact asphalt containing waste glass. Field testing should follow the procedures used for conventional hot mix asphalt. The guidance identifies a need for uniform specifications covering sizing, debris levels, and mix limitations. It says a lack of adequate and consistent glass supply remains a major constraint on wider use.
Article Summary: At least 17 streets in Baltimore were paved with recycled glass. Glass can replace some of the conventional aggregate used in road construction. New York City used about 225,000 metric tonnes of glass in resurfacing applications between 1990 and 1995. Earlier projects found problems when glass was used in high percentages or as large pieces.

Article Title: 'Terrible thing': Trump on Riyadh airport attack, says US may join Saudi strikes against Yemen’s Houthis
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump speaks to reporters as he weighs joining Saudi Arabia’s strikes against Yemen’s Houthi rebels following a deadly attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport

US warns citizens against travelling to Riyadh airport

Airport attack kills 12, injures over 300

US President Donald Trump said Washington was considering joining Saudi Arabia’s strikes against Yemen’s Houthi rebels after an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 12 people and injured more than 300, according to Saudi civil aviation authorities.Asked whether he had decided to join the Saudi strikes, Trump said, “We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack. We will make a decision. We move very quickly.”He added, “Look, the Saudis are good fighters. But I think the attack was a terrible thing.”The attack on Saturday was the deadliest in a Gulf country since the start of the Iran war, as fighting has expanded to include renewed clashes between Iran-backed Houthi rebels and Saudi-backed government forces in Yemen.The US Mission in Saudi Arabia issued a security alert on Sunday, urging American citizens to avoid King Khalid International Airport and surrounding areas following the October 10 attacks.It also advised travellers to exercise extreme caution at major Saudi airports and warned of possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruptions. Passengers were advised to check their flight status directly with airlines and airports.The mission said US government employees in Saudi Arabia required special authorisation to use King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, as well as airports in Jeddah and Dammam.The latest attacks are expected to intensify pressure on Saudi Arabia’s allies, including the US, to provide military support as the kingdom steps up its campaign against the Houthis.Saudi civil aviation authorities said the dead included four Saudi citizens and nationals of Bangladesh, Palestine, the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria and Sudan. The injured were being treated at several hospitals, with some in critical condition.A missile struck a complex housing terminals 3 and 4, used for domestic flights, a regional official said, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak to the media.The attack was the latest in a series of strikes targeting King Khalid International Airport over the past week. The Houthis had claimed responsibility for earlier attacks on the airport that killed three Saudis, including a pilot.The surge in attacks has also targeted other Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure, following a major military offensive launched against the Houthis by a Saudi-led coalition last week.
Article Summary: US warns citizens against travelling to Riyadh airport following deadly attack. Airport attack kills 12, injures over 300, according to Saudi civil aviation authorities. The attack on Saturday was the deadliest in a Gulf country since the start of the Iran war.

Article Title: In 2015, James Patterson pledged $1.25 million to US school libraries; after requests poured in, he raised his gift to $1.75 million, helping 467 libraries fund books, reading programmes and repairs
Article Text:
James Patterson raised his 2015 school library donation to $1.75m, helping 467 US libraries (Image Credit: ALA)

A pledge to help school libraries

Why the donation increased

How 467 school libraries benefited

Recognition for a wider literacy effort

A flood of requests from schools revealed how badly many libraries needed support, prompting bestselling author James Patterson to increase a donation he had originally planned at $1.25 million. In March 2015, Patterson announced the pledge in partnership with Scholastic Reading Club to help US school libraries buy books and improve their resources. According to the American Association of School Librarians (AASL), the overwhelming response led him to raise the total to $1.75 million, with 467 school libraries eventually receiving grants. The funding could support books, reading programmes, technology and repairs, addressing practical needs that affect how children access reading and learning resources.Patterson announced the initiative on March 9, 2015, working with Scholastic Reading Club to distribute grants to schools across the United States. The programme was designed to make funding accessible to school libraries, with individual grants ranging from $1,000 to $10,000. The author said he was concerned that fewer children were growing up in homes filled with books. He believed access to books and functioning school libraries could influence children's education and encourage a lasting interest in reading.Scholastic Reading Club helped administer applications through its network of schools and teachers. It also offered recipients additional purchasing support through its Bonus Points programme, which teachers could use to obtain books and classroom materials. The partnership connected Patterson's personal donation with an established education network, allowing the money to reach schools that needed help with their library resources.The response to the announcement was far greater than anticipated. Within two weeks, Patterson and Scholastic had received more than 8,500 applications, according to a March 23, 2015, Scholastic announcement. The volume of requests prompted Patterson to add $250,000 to his original pledge, taking the total to $1.5 million. Demand continued to grow. By June 2015, the partners had received more than 28,000 applications. Patterson then announced another $250,000 increase, bringing the donation to $1.75 million.The requests highlighted a range of problems facing school libraries. Schools sought money for new books, shelving, classroom materials and repairs, including damage caused by flooding. Others needed resources to improve the spaces in which students read and studied. The response also gave Patterson and Scholastic an opportunity to draw attention to the challenges schools faced in maintaining well-stocked libraries. The programme was intended not only to distribute grants but also to highlight the importance of access to books and reading resources.The grants were distributed in stages during 2015. In June, Patterson and Scholastic announced the first round of awards, distributing $500,000 among 127 schools. Individual grants ranged from $1,000 to $10,000, while the remaining funds were scheduled for distribution later in the year. The American Association of School Librarians reported in March 2016 that 467 school libraries had received funding through the programme. According to the organisation, the grants supported books, reading programmes, technology and repairs.These areas of spending addressed different needs. New books could expand the material available to students, while reading programmes could help schools encourage children to develop stronger reading habits. Technology could improve access to educational resources, and repairs could help keep library spaces usable. For schools working with limited resources, even a relatively small grant could address a specific need. The programme allowed libraries to identify their priorities and request funding accordingly, rather than requiring every recipient to spend the money in the same way.Patterson's support for school libraries was part of a broader effort to encourage reading among children. In March 2016, the AASL selected him as the recipient of its Crystal Apple award, recognising his contribution to school library programmes and students. The organisation noted his financial support as well as his advocacy for librarians and reading. Patterson said his aim was to make books available to children in every neighbourhood and encourage them to become lifelong readers.His partnership with Scholastic also continued beyond the original campaign. In November 2016, the two announced another $1.75 million in school library grants, this time supporting 452 schools. Patterson subsequently extended his education and literacy initiatives to classroom libraries and other programmes. The 2015 pledge demonstrated how a donation can grow when the demand for support becomes clear. What began as a $1.25 million commitment became a $1.75 million programme that helped hundreds of school libraries address their needs, while bringing wider attention to the role libraries play in children's education.
Article Summary: Patterson announced the initiative on March 9, 2015. He worked with Scholastic Reading Club to distribute grants to schools. The grants supported books, reading programmes, technology and repairs. The American Association of School Librarians reported in March 2016 that 467 school libraries had received funding.

Article Title: Meet Stephen Biebelhausen, the US doctor who pushed his 1-year-old daughter in a pram and accidentally broke a world record
Article Text:
Image: Washington Post

A race that became a world-record attempt

He finished in 4 minutes 17.784 seconds

Blake was already his running partner

He had little specific preparation

His daughter was there for the record

Stephen Biebelhausen, a 30-year-old US emergency medicine physician and former college runner, was aiming for a fast mile when he entered Cleveland's Guardian Mile with his one-year-old daughter, Blake, in a stroller. He hoped to beat the event's 4-minute 44-second course record, but did not expect to challenge the world record. During the race, however, he realised he was running faster than the existing mark and began pushing harder. Biebelhausen finished the mile in 4 minutes 17.784 seconds on August 8, 2026, setting the Guinness World Records title for the fastest mile pushing a pram by a male. He improved the previous world record of 4:26.29 by about 8.5 seconds.The Guardian Mile is an annual one-mile race held across Cleveland's Hope Memorial Bridge in Ohio. Biebelhausen entered its stroller division with Blake, initially focused on having a good run with his daughter and trying to surpass the course record of 4 minutes 44 seconds. He knew the existing world record was 4 minutes 26.29 seconds, but Guinness World Records reports that he considered that mark out of reach before the race.As the race unfolded, his pace changed his expectations. He completed the first 400 metres in 65 seconds and reached the halfway point in 2 minutes 12 seconds. Having looked up the world record beforehand, he realised at halfway that he was ahead of the required pace and decided to push harder.Biebelhausen crossed the finish line in 4:17.784, setting the official Guinness World Records title for the fastest mile pushing a pram by a male. The official Guinness listing gives August 8, 2026, as the date and Cleveland, Ohio, as the location.The previous record was 4:26.29, achieved by Silas Frantz while pushing his son Otto in Arroyo Grande, California, on June 24, 2025. Biebelhausen therefore lowered the record by about 8.5 seconds. His time also surpassed the Guardian Mile's 4:44 course record.The record-breaking race was not Biebelhausen's first time running with Blake. He told Guinness World Records that he normally takes three or four easy runs with his daughter each week. He said Blake enjoys the outings and becomes happy when the stroller is put in the car or when they arrive at one of their usual running locations.Biebelhausen also said running gives him time to get away, reset and recharge from a fast-moving life. He described running with Blake as making the mental side of the activity easier because she is often laughing and giggling. He acknowledged that pushing the stroller makes running physically harder, but said her enjoyment makes the effort worthwhile.Despite setting a world record, Biebelhausen said he had not undertaken an extensive training programme specifically for the stroller mile. He normally ran with Blake several times a week, and he completed just one workout at mile pace during the week before the Guardian Mile.He said the purpose of that workout was to make sure Blake was comfortable with going that fast and that he felt safe running at that pace while pushing her. After that, the father and daughter simply turned up for the race.Biebelhausen was already an experienced runner. Miami University's athletics records show that he competed in track and cross-country for the RedHawks and recorded a personal best of 4:15.80 for the indoor mile, 3:48.11 for 1,500 metres and 14:55.49 for 5,000 metres. He graduated from Miami with a 3.51 GPA in bioengineering and premedical studies.Biebelhausen's wife, Meghan, watched from the sidelines. Guinness World Records reports that when Stephen reached the finish and raised his hands, Meghan realised he had achieved the world record. She described the moment as a shock but said she was excited for both of them.The achievement was especially meaningful because Biebelhausen had entered the race primarily to enjoy the experience with his daughter. Blake, who was one year old at the time, remained in the stroller throughout the mile. What began as a father-daughter run therefore ended with an official Guinness World Records title, giving the family an unusual story to share with Blake as she grows older.
Article Summary: Stephen Biebelhausen entered Cleveland's Guardian Mile with his one-year-old daughter, Blake, in a stroller. He hoped to beat the event's 4-minute 44-second course record, but did not expect to challenge the world record. During the race, however, he realised he was running faster than the existing mark and began pushing harder. He crossed the finish line in 4:17.784, setting the official Guinness World Records title for the fastest mile pushing a pram by a male.

Article Title: Harvard bought this stained document for $27.50; decades later, experts realised it was an original Magna Carta
Article Text:
Spectral imaging expert Bill Christens-Barry and Debora Mayor of the Weissman Preservation Centre Prepare HLS MS172 for imaging. Image Credit: Harvard Law Today

Harvard ’s $27.50 Magna Carta remained unrecognised for decades

Magna Carta scholar David Carpenter of King's College London examines the digitised document. Image Credit: Isobel Sheeran, King's College London/Harvard Law Today

What first revealed the document’s true identity

Why the edition from 1300 was so important

How did scholars confirm the parchment was genuine

Experts examined the document using spectral imaging. Image Credit: Harvard Law School

Where had Harvard’s Magna Carta come from

Harvard Law School bought a stained and faded parchment in 1946 for just $27.50, believing it was an ordinary later copy of the Magna Carta. The document was catalogued as dating from 1327 and remained in the library for decades. Nearly 80 years later, medieval historians examining a digital image noticed that something about it did not fit that description. Further research and specialist imaging eventually showed that the parchment was an original version issued by King Edward I in 1300, making it one of only seven surviving copies of that edition.The document, identified as HLS MS 172, had long been treated as an unremarkable copy. Harvard Law School’s records show that the library bought it in 1946 for $27.50 after it had been sold through a London book dealer. The auction catalogue described it as a copy made in 1327 that was somewhat rubbed and damp-stained, a description that helped keep its true age hidden for generations. Smithsonian Magazine reported that the London dealer Sweet & Maxwell had bought the parchment at Sotheby’s for £42 only about a month before Harvard acquired it.The parchment measures about 489 by 473 millimetres, or roughly 19 inches by 19 inches.It was part of Harvard Law School Library’s collection of historic documents and had even been placed on display. Digital images were also available online, meaning the document was not completely hidden from researchers. Its significance, however, remained unnoticed until a medieval historian happened to examine those images. ABC News reported that library staff had continued to regard it as a cheap copy even while it was on display.David Carpenter, a professor of medieval history at King’s College London, was studying digitised Magna Carta material in December 2023 when he came across HLS MS 172 on Harvard’s website. The handwriting, layout and overall appearance immediately suggested to him that the parchment could be an original from 1300 rather than the later copy recorded in the catalogue. He then contacted Nicholas Vincent, a medieval historian at the University of East Anglia, to help investigate.The researchers had several clues to examine. Harvard Law School reported that the document’s dimensions matched those of the 6 previously known originals from 1300. Its handwriting also showed distinctive features, including a large capital E at the beginning of Edwardus and elongated letters in the opening line. Those details were consistent with the other surviving originals.The researchers then faced a more difficult problem. Much of the writing had faded, making a direct comparison challenging. Harvard librarians used ultraviolet light and spectral imaging to reveal details that could not be seen clearly with the naked eye. The scans made it possible to examine the faded writing and compare the document closely with the other known originals from 1300.The Magna Carta had first been issued in 1215 under King John and established a lasting principle that the monarch was subject to the law. The charter later became an important influence on constitutional traditions in Britain and elsewhere, including the development of the United States’ founding documents. ABC News noted that several updated editions followed the original, including the version issued by Edward I in 1300.That 1300 edition is particularly significant because it was the last time the full Magna Carta was set out and authorised by the king’s seal. According to PBS NewsHour, it was the 6th and final version in a sequence of editions issued after the original, while Smithsonian Magazine described Edward I’s 1300 reissue as the last time an English king confirmed the Magna Carta.Before Harvard’s discovery, six original copies from the 1300 issue were known. The identification of HLS MS 172 therefore increased that number to 7. Harvard Law School said the document is now recognised as one of only seven surviving originals from that particular issue.Carpenter and Vincent did not rely simply on its appearance. They compared the text against the other originals and found that it matched the authorised wording. Harvard Law School reported that the seven documents were examined alongside one another and that the clerks who produced them had been instructed to follow a prepared text closely. Any significant difference could therefore have raised doubts about the Harvard parchment.Instead, the document passed the comparison with extremely strong results. Ultraviolet and spectral images helped reveal writing that had become difficult to see over time, allowing the researchers to compare the wording closely. PBS reported that the scholars also examined the handwriting and the physical dimensions, finding them consistent with the known originals.The discovery also changed the estimated importance of what had been sitting in Harvard’s collection. Carpenter estimated that the parchment could be worth millions of dollars. A 1297 Magna Carta sold for $21.3 million at auction in 2007, although Harvard has no plans to sell its newly authenticated document.Authenticating the parchment was only part of the mystery. Vincent also investigated its earlier history and traced a possible route back to Appleby in Westmorland, England. Harvard Law School reported that the document was sent to auction in 1945 by First World War flying ace Forster Sammy Maynard.Maynard had inherited archives connected with Thomas and John Clarkson, prominent campaigners against the slave trade. Thomas Clarkson had later retired to the English Lake District and became friendly with William Wordsworth and William Lowther, who was associated with Appleby. Researchers believe the Magna Carta may have passed from Appleby through the Lowthers and Clarksons before reaching Maynard and eventually the auction market.That final part of the story is not completely proven. Vincent said the evidence strongly suggests that Harvard’s parchment could be the lost Magna Carta once issued to Appleby, but further documentation would be needed to establish the connection conclusively.
Article Summary: Harvard Law School bought a stained and faded parchment in 1946 for just $27.50. The document was catalogued as dating from 1327 and remained in the library for decades. Medieval historians examining a digital image noticed that something about it did not fit that description. Further research and specialist imaging eventually showed that the parchment was an original version issued by King Edward I in 1300.

Article Title: In 2012, Taylor Swift pledged $4 million for a Nashville education centre; 14 years later, the space is showcasing artwork by local schoolchildren and artists with developmental disabilities
Article Text:
Taylor Swift

A major gift for education

Taylor Swift’s ‘Patient Zero’ mansion: Inside the $47 million Beverly Hills home where her music video was filmed(Image Credit: Instagram)

Learning by making

Two groups, one exhibition

A centre still doing its job

From a pledge to a public platform

Taylor Swift’s $4 million gift to the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum in 2012 helped create a dedicated education centre in Nashville. The space was designed for more than music lessons: it would give children and families room to learn, experiment and engage with country music’s history. Fourteen years later, the centre is hosting Connection, an exhibition of posters created by Metro Nashville Public Schools students and artists from Friends Life Community, a nonprofit serving adults with developmental disabilities. The museum says the participants explored the history and techniques of Hatch Show Print, its historic letterpress shop, before making their own work. The exhibition brings the centre’s original educational promise to life, showing how a space built for learning can keep opening doors to creativity and community.In May 2012, Swift pledged $4 million towards a new education centre at the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. According to MusicRow, it was the largest capital contribution by an individual artist in the museum’s 45-year history at the time. The museum named the centre in her honour.The gift formed part of a wider expansion campaign called 'Working on a Building: Country Music Lives Here'. The museum planned to grow from 140,000 square feet to more than 350,000 square feet, creating additional exhibition and learning spaces as well as new visitor facilities.The Taylor Swift Education Center was planned as a space of more than 7,500 square feet, spread across parts of two floors. Its design included three classrooms and a children’s exhibition gallery. The museum expected its new facilities to increase its educational capacity by as much as sevenfold.The planned classrooms were intended for a range of activities, from the museum’s flagship Words & Music programme to family events and distance learning. One “wet classroom” was designed for hands-on projects that could get messy, including letterpress art activities connected to Hatch Show Print.The centre’s original vision was not limited to traditional classroom instruction. The museum planned spaces where students could explore objects, observe curators at work and take part in activities that made music history tangible. A visible storage area and design studio would allow visitors to see how museum professionals handle and interpret collections.That hands-on approach is reflected in the centre’s current exhibition, Connection. Opened in 2026, the show brings together posters made by Metro Nashville Public Schools students and artists engaged with Friends Life Community. The project began with visits to Hatch Show Print, the museum’s nearly 150-year-old letterpress shop. Students learned about the shop’s history, studied design principles and explored how letterpress printing works. They then created shapes using foam and sponges, printed those forms and used them as inspiration for their finished posters, as per reports.The process gave participants a chance to learn not only by looking at art, but by making it. They experimented with words, images, colour and composition, using the print shop’s techniques to develop their own visual ideas.The exhibition also grew from a collaboration between the museum and Friends Life Community, which serves adults with developmental disabilities. Friends Life invited Hatch Show Print Master Printer Emeritus Jim Sherraden to work as a teaching artist in residence in 2023. In late 2024, artists from Friends Life Community visited the print shop for a behind-the-presses tour. Sherraden and Jennifer Haston, the organisation’s visual arts programme coordinator, helped participants bring their words, lettering and images to life through poster-making, as per reports.The posters created by both groups form the exhibition’s central focus. The museum says the works use action words and imagery to imagine a future where people connect through creative art and social causes. The title Connection speaks to the ideas behind the exhibition, but also to the relationships built through the process: between students and artists, participants and printers, and the public and the museum.The project demonstrates how a museum education space can bring people together across ages and abilities. It also gives visitors the opportunity to encounter work made by members of their own community, rather than only by established artists or historical figures.When Swift made her pledge, the museum described the centre as a place for school groups, families, young people and adults. The new exhibition shows how that original ambition continues to shape the space more than a decade later.The education centre is not simply a room named after a famous musician. It is part of the museum’s broader effort to connect people with country music and its creative traditions through participation. In Connection, that means learning about letterpress printing, trying the process and producing posters that reflect the creators’ own ideas.The exhibition is open to museum visitors, with admission included in the price of a museum ticket. The museum also offers free admission for local youth and discounted tickets for up to two accompanying adults from Davidson County and neighbouring counties, with proof of residency.Swift’s generous contribution of $4 million played a crucial role in creating a lasting educational component within one of Nashville’s most iconic cultural institutions. The carefully designed classrooms, a dedicated children’s gallery, and interactive programming were all put in place with the intention of transforming the museum into more than just a location for viewing exhibitions. These elements were strategically crafted to provide visitors with opportunities to learn through hands-on experiences and active participation.Fast forward a remarkable fourteen years, and the vibrant and eye-catching posters showcased in the current exhibition, aptly titled Connection, stand as a compelling testament to that original vision which has been successfully brought to life. Local students, in collaboration with talented artists who have developmental disabilities, have engaged deeply in the exploration of a historic printing tradition. They have successfully harnessed this medium to express and convey their unique perspectives and personal narratives.However, it is important to note that this exhibition does not represent the conclusion of the center's evolving narrative. Instead, it serves to illustrate the extraordinary outcomes that can arise when a cultural institution commits resources and efforts toward creating a dedicated physical space, fostering educational opportunities, and promoting creative accessibility over an extended timeframe. A generous gift made in 2012 laid a solid foundation for establishing this creative setting; now, the individuals who engage with it today are actively populating that environment with their own creative works, innovative ideas, and meaningful connections.
Article Summary: In May 2012, Swift pledged $4 million towards a new education centre at the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum in Nashville. Fourteen years later, the centre is hosting Connection, an exhibition of posters created by Metro Nashville Public Schools students and artists from Friends Life Community.

Article Title: After a New York fire killed a 13-year-old girl's father and four sisters, relatives raised over $100,000 for her; months later, the state AG sought $71,539.29 it said remained unpaid
Article Text:
A community came together after the tragedy

How the donations came under scrutiny

State sought the return of more than $71,000

A New York teenager who lost her father and four sisters in a devastating house fire was at the centre of a legal dispute months later, after relatives who raised more than $100,000 to support her allegedly failed to hand over most of the money. According to a 2019 report by WWNY-TV and court documents cited by the broadcaster, the New York Attorney General’s office sought the return of $71,539.29, alleging that the funds had been improperly spent and that investigators had been misled about the money. The case was filed in New York State Supreme Court in October 2019 by then-Attorney General Letitia James. The state alleged that the relatives had not transferred the full amount to Hailey or her mother, Melissa Davey, despite repeated requests for an accounting. The original court petition also alleged that the fundraisers had failed to comply with state requirements governing charitable donations. WWNY-TV⁠ and the court petition⁠ detailed the allegations.The fire broke out on February 14, 2019, at the family’s home on Myrtle Avenue in Watertown, New York. Hailey’s father, Aaron Bodah, and her four sisters, Merissa, Alexa, Erin and Skylar, died in the blaze. Hailey, then 13, was the only surviving child in the family.The tragedy prompted an outpouring of support from the local community. A GoFundMe campaign organised on behalf of Kenneth Bodah raised $25,680 through 523 donations, according to the fundraising page⁠ . Other efforts included community fundraisers and donations collected through a memorial fund and a union-related initiative.The fundraising was intended to help Hailey following the loss of her immediate family. In a letter published in the local newspaper, her paternal relatives had reportedly assured donors that the money would be managed responsibly and used for her benefit, according to the state’s court filing.The Attorney General’s office began seeking financial records after learning that the funds had not been transferred to Hailey or her mother within the period specified under state law. According to the petition, the relatives were asked in August 2019 to disclose the total amount raised, identify where the money was being held and explain how the funds would be handed over. A cashier’s cheque for $35,021.61 was delivered to Hailey on September 20, 2019, through the relatives’ lawyer.However, investigators subsequently obtained bank records that showed $97,199.29 had been deposited into an account called the Bodah Family Memorial Fund between February 19 and September 23, 2019. The state alleged that a substantial portion of the money remained unaccounted for or had been spent on purchases that were not consistent with the stated purpose of the fundraising.The records cited in the petition included more than $5,300 in purchases from Lowe’s, a home improvement retailer, covering household appliances and other supplies. A further $453.86 was spent at an online home furnishings retailer, according to the filing. The state also identified payments to a church and a monument company. It argued that the donations had been solicited specifically for Hailey and that the money should not have been diverted to other expenses without the appropriate basis.By October 2019, the Attorney General’s office was seeking the transfer of the remaining $71,539.29 to Hailey, through her mother and legal guardian. It also requested penalties and a full accounting of the money raised through the different fundraising efforts.Kenneth Bodah Jr., Beth Ann Bodah and Travis Bodah were accused of failing to turn over the donations as required by law. The petition further accused Kenneth and Beth of making false statements to investigators, while Kenneth was separately accused of fraud.These were allegations contained in the state’s legal filing, rather than findings of guilt. WWNY-TV reported at the time that it had been unable to reach the three relatives for comment. The case highlighted the questions that can arise when donations are collected for a named individual after a tragedy, particularly when relatives or other organisers control the funds before they reach the intended beneficiary. In Hailey’s case, the state sought to ensure that the money raised in the aftermath of an unimaginable loss was delivered to the teenager it was meant to support.
Article Summary: Hailey Bodah lost her father and four sisters in a house fire in February 2019. The tragedy prompted an outpouring of support from the local community. A GoFundMe campaign organised on behalf of Kenneth Bodah raised $25,680 through 523 donations, according to the fundraising page. Other efforts included community fundraisers and donations collected through a memorial fund and a union-related initiative. The fundraising was intended to help Hailey following the loss of her immediate family. The state alleged that the relatives had not transferred the full amount to Hailey or her mother, Melissa Davey.

Article Title: 'As one of the largest research universities...': Arizona State responds to federal probe into J-1 visa use after JD Vance says 'something weird is going on'
Article Text:
Arizona State University reacts to JD Vance's probe.

Why is the US investigating ASU and eight other universities?

What is the J-1 visa programme?

Arizona State University has defended its hiring practices after the Trump administration launched a federal investigation into the use of J-1 visas at nine major US universities, with Vice President JD Vance alleging that the programme was being used to undercut wages for American researchers.ASU said it had hired the talent needed to support its research and academic operations in full compliance with US laws and policies. The university was among nine institutions named by Vance during an October 8 news conference announcing a new federal crackdown on alleged visa fraud.“As one of the largest research universities in the United States, Arizona State University educates more STEM majors than any other university, and employs one of the largest technical and scientific workforces in the country,” the university said in a statement. “This benefits both the Arizona and the United States economies, and in doing so, ASU has hired the talent needed to perform these functions, and done so in complete compliance with existing United States policy and law. ”The investigation is part of a broader Trump administration effort to scrutinise the use of employment and exchange-visitor visa programmes. US Department of Labor Inspector General Anthony D’Esposito said subpoenas had already been served and investigations were under way.Vance named Harvard University, Yale University, Stanford University, Brown University, the University of Pittsburgh, the University of California, Davis, the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), ASU and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) as institutions requiring scrutiny.The vice president alleged that the universities relied disproportionately on J-1 visa holders for federally funded research positions, potentially allowing them to pay less than they would pay American graduate students and researchers.According to figures cited by Vance, J-1 visa holders accounted for approximately 61% of research positions supported by federal grants at the nine institutions, compared with a national average of about 38%. He also claimed that American graduate students and researchers earned around $20,000 more than individuals brought in under the J-1 programme.“Something weird is going on at these universities,” Vance said, arguing that the programme was being used to reduce labour costs at the expense of American workers.The allegations have not established that ASU or the other universities violated immigration law. The investigation is intended to examine whether the institutions improperly used visa classifications and federal research funding.The J-1 visa is a non-immigrant visa for individuals participating in designated exchange programmes in the United States. It covers categories including research scholars, professors, students and other exchange visitors.Universities and research institutions use the programme to bring international scholars and researchers to the US for academic exchange, teaching and research.Unlike the H-1B visa, which allows employers to hire foreign workers in specialty occupations, the J-1 is specifically designed for approved exchange-visitor activities. Its rules and eligibility requirements differ from those governing H-1B employment.The Trump administration's investigation focuses on whether universities have used the J-1 programme in ways that circumvent employment obligations, depress wages or improperly benefit from taxpayer-funded research.D’Esposito said the government would examine whether foreign influence, improper financial relationships or visa-related misconduct had compromised federally funded research.
Article Summary: ASU said it had hired the talent needed to support its research and academic operations in full compliance with US laws and policies. The university was among nine institutions named by JD Vance during an October 8 news conference announcing a new federal crackdown on alleged visa fraud. The investigation is intended to examine whether the institutions improperly used visa classifications and federal research funding.

Article Title: Strong pushback as US downgrades Hong Kong to tier-3 in human trafficking: 'Double standard'
Article Text:
US downgrades Hong Kong to tier 3 in the human trafficking ranking.

What the US report said about Hong Kong

Hong Kong has rejected the United States’ decision to place it in the lowest category of its annual human trafficking report, calling the assessment “entirely unfounded” and accusing Washington of applying double standards in evaluating the city’s efforts to combat trafficking. The US State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, released on October 8, downgraded Hong Kong to Tier 3 from the Tier 2 Watch List, where it had remained for two consecutive years. The lowest tier includes mainland China, Macau, North Korea, Russia, Iran and Afghanistan.In a statement, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government strongly rejected the assessment, describing it as an attempt to damage the city’s reputation. It maintained that human trafficking had never been prevalent in Hong Kong and disputed the US assertion that the city was not making significant efforts to eliminate the crime.The US report, however, said Hong Kong did not fully meet the minimum standards for eliminating trafficking and had fallen short in prosecuting suspected traffickers and identifying victims exploited within the territory.The tier rankings assess governments’ efforts to combat human trafficking, rather than the prevalence of trafficking itself.According to the report, Hong Kong authorities investigated 11 human trafficking cases in 2025, all involving forced labour, compared with seven cases in 2024. However, authorities prosecuted one suspect, down from two the previous year, while two sex traffickers were convicted. One of those convicted received a prison sentence of less than a year.The report also raised concerns about victim identification. Despite conducting approximately 12,100 initial screenings in 2025, authorities identified no victims who had been exploited within Hong Kong.All 15 victims identified during the year were Hong Kong residents who had fallen prey to employment fraud and been forced to work in scam centres in Myanmar and Cambodia, the report said.The Hong Kong government confirmed the screening and victim figures but said the number of screenings had increased by 7 per cent from the previous year. It argued that bringing residents home safely, identifying them as trafficking victims and investigating those implicated demonstrated its commitment to tackling the crime.A government spokesman accused the US of hypocrisy, citing studies and reports that had highlighted the underreporting of human trafficking cases by American law enforcement agencies.The US report reiterated its criticism that Hong Kong lacks a single law criminalising all forms of human trafficking. Instead, authorities rely on a range of offences relating to prostitution, immigration, employment and physical abuse.The Hong Kong government defended its legal framework, saying more than 50 legal provisions address trafficking-related conduct and provide safeguards comparable to those available under dedicated anti-trafficking legislation in other jurisdictions.“There is simply no one-size-fits-all solution,” the government spokesman said.The report criticized Hong Kong’s rules governing foreign domestic workers, particularly the live-in requirement and the “two-week rule”, which generally requires workers whose employment ends to leave Hong Kong within two weeks unless they obtain permission to remain.According to the US assessment, these arrangements could increase workers’ vulnerability to exploitation by employers and employment agencies. It also raised concerns that agencies routinely charged fees exceeding the legal limit and that penalties were insufficient to deter violations.Hong Kong has approximately 380,000 foreign domestic workers.Defending the arrangements, the Hong Kong government said the live-in requirement supported its policy of giving local workers priority in employment. It added that domestic workers who experienced abuse or exploitation could apply to change employers without first returning to their home countries.The government said employment agencies could charge workers no more than 10 per cent of their first month’s salary following successful placement. It also cited more than 1,700 inspections of domestic worker employment agencies in 2025 and the arrest of 37 employers in connection with physical or sexual abuse of domestic workers.
Article Summary: The US State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, released on October 8, downgraded Hong Kong to Tier 3 from the Tier 2 Watch List. The lowest tier includes mainland China, Macau, North Korea, Russia, Iran and Afghanistan.

Article Title: Pak crisis: Shehbaz govt declares emergency, ends Imran Khan's party's rule in KPK
Article Text:
PTI has been mobilising supporters to pressure the federal government over Khan's imprisonment

Terrorism, law and order cited

PTI protests, warns of bloodshed

Pakistan on Sunday declared an emergency in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK), suspending the provincial government led by jailed former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party amid deteriorating law and order and a growing confrontation with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government.President Asif Ali Zardari issued the proclamation under Articles 232(1) and 234(1) of the Constitution, citing rising terrorist attacks and a breakdown of constitutional machinery in the province. The move strips the elected provincial administration of its powers, with the chief minister, provincial ministers, advisers, special assistants and advocate general required to vacate their offices.The decision comes as thousands of PTI supporters march towards Islamabad, demanding Khan's release and access to medical treatment for the former prime minister, who has been in prison since 2023 on corruption and other charges. The party has described the cases against him as politically motivated. The emergency also follows failed negotiations between PTI and the federal government over the planned protest.The presidential declaration said the emergency had been imposed because of the grave security situation and the provincial government's alleged failure to tackle militancy.“The extraordinary intensity of terrorist incidents poses serious threats to the lives and property of the public,” the declaration stated.PTI has been mobilising supporters to pressure the federal government over Khan's imprisonment. KPK chief minister Sohail Afridi is leading the protest march, which began in Lakki Marwat on October 4 and has passed through several districts.The party had initially planned to take the march to Islamabad for a sit-in, but authorities have erected roadblocks using shipping containers at entry points to the capital and other locations. Two rounds of talks between PTI and the government failed to break the deadlock.Zulfikar Bukhari, a close Khan aide and PTI spokesman, called the emergency a “ridiculous decision”, saying KPK had the country's “only legitimately elected government”.“This will only lead to further bloodshed, instability and collateral damage,” he said, adding that there had always been room for talks but the decision showed negotiations were never the government's intention.Previous protests by Khan's supporters have turned violent, with security personnel and civilians killed during demonstrations in 2024.
Article Summary: President Asif Ali Zardari declares emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Suspends provincial government led by Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party. Decision comes as thousands of PTI supporters march towards Islamabad, demanding Khan's release.

Article Title: ‘No contact, no update’: Imran Khan’s son says father silent for 6 months, aunts remain ‘abducted’
Article Text:
Imran Khan's son warns against Adiala jail protest

Kasim says protests will continue

Sisters detained ahead of PTI protest

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan’s son Kasim Khan has claimed that his three aunts remain “abducted” by Pakistani authorities, saying their family and lawyers have received no information about their condition or the reasons for their detention. He also said he and his brother have had no contact with their father for more than six months.Kasim Khan made the remarks on Thursday, weeks after his aunts Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) planned September 27 protest and march to Islamabad.The demonstrations were called to demand updates on Imran Khan's health and his release from Adiala Jail, where the former prime minister has been incarcerated since August 2023.In a post on X, Kasim Khan linked the continued detention of his aunts with the lack of contact with his father."Currently, my Aunties are still abducted. Family and lawyers have received no update on how they are, nor why they are incarcerated. Concerning my father, there is complete silence. My brother and I have had no contact with him for more than six months. We do not even know the true state of his health," the post read.Kasim Khan also referred to protests being held in Pakistan over his father's imprisonment, saying people were continuing to demand justice and the right to be heard."Meanwhile, thousands of Pakistanis are peacefully taking to the streets to protest against his illegal and politically motivated imprisonment. However, the people of Pakistan have not given up. No barricade, intimidation or repression can muzzle the people’s demand for justice and their democratic right to be heard. There can be no lasting peace or stability while their democratic will is suppressed and their chosen leader remains behind bars,” Kasim Khan added.His remarks came a day after the families of the three detained sisters approached the Lahore High Court seeking permission for relatives and lawyers to meet them.According to Dawn, Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar filed two civil miscellaneous applications in pending writ petitions on behalf of Shah Raiz Khan, son of Aleema Khan, and Sakeena Niazi, daughter of Noreen Niazi.The pleas challenged the denial of meetings between the detained women and their family members and lawyers, and also raised the issue of access to medicines.The families have alleged that neither relatives nor legal counsel have been permitted to meet the three women or provide them with medicines. The applications stated that medicines had been provided to the sisters on only one occasion and that no one had subsequently been allowed to meet them, Dawn reported.The pleas have sought directions from the Lahore High Court allowing family members and lawyers to meet the detained women and provide them with medicines, according to Dawn.Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of PTI's September 27 protest call.The detentions came amid a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its planned countrywide demonstrations and march to Islamabad. The party had called for the protests to demand Imran Khan's release and mobilise support for the supremacy of the Constitution.On September 24, the Lahore High Court had declined a request to immediately suspend notifications ordering the preventive detention of the three sisters.Imran Khan has been in Adiala Jail since August 2023. His detention and the PTI's protests have remained at the centre of a wider political confrontation in Pakistan, with the party continuing to demand his release.
Article Summary: Kasim Khan claims his three aunts remain 'abducted' by Pakistani authorities. He also says he and his brother have had no contact with their father for six months. His aunts Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were detained for 30 days ahead of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) planned September 27 protest.

Article Title: Pak army chief Munir bypasses PM Sharif, moves to deploy more military assets to Saudi Arabia
Article Text:
Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is built on on a 2025 Saudi-Pakistani pact under which Pakistan had sent about 8,000 troops to the kingdom by May (Photo: Agencies).

Pakistan defence forces chief Asim Munir agreed to quickly deploy more Pakistani troops to Saudi Arabia , despite the Pakistani Parliament voting to stay out of the Houthi conflict 11 years ago.The Mecca defence pact signed by Pakistan with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August was invoked for the first time on Monday, amid increasing Houthi attacks on the Saudi kingdom.According to Reuters, the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is based on a 2025 Saudi-Pakistani pact under which Pakistan had sent about 8,000 troops to the kingdom by May.Pakistan's information ministry said the alliance "has gone through all necessary government procedures".However, it did not clarify if the cabinet or parliament was involved, calling details of the deployment "a matter ​of operational confidentiality."Senior fellow for South Asia at the Atlantic ​Council, Michael Kugelman, told Reuters that Pakistan is currently in a different era, with a comparatively weaker parliament."There were times in the past when Pakistan's parliament would vote not to send ⁠troops, and the military would abide by that decision. But it's a different era now," Kugelman said.Pakistan's armed forces have often been accused of holding the reins of Islamabad’s politics.In 2025, Munir was elected as the field marshal, the chief of all defence forces in Pakistan. Constitutional changes have allowed him to hold the position till 2030, with lifetime rank as the field marshal.Munir is also immune to any criminal prosecution, signalling the military's increasing influence over the constitutional establishment.Munir is widely acknowledged to be more powerful domestically than any of his predecessors. The military has control over major government portfolios like defence and foreign relations.Jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan ’s party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), currently protesting for his release, has accused the army of dominating politics.The relationship between Imran Khan and Asim Munir has reportedly been bitter since 2019, when Munir, then director-general of Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), was removed after less than eight months in the post, reportedly at the insistence of the then-PM Khan.No official reason was given for Munir’s removal.Khan was himself ousted as prime minister in April 2022. Seven months later, in November 2022, Munir returned to the centre of Pakistan’s power structure when PM Shehbaz Sharif appointed him army chief, succeeding Bajwa.
Article Summary: Pakistan's armed forces have often been accused of holding the reins of Islamabad’s politics. Mecca defence pact signed by Pakistan with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in August was invoked for the first time on Monday. Pakistan's information ministry said the alliance "has gone through all necessary government procedures"

Article Title: Pakistan bets on electric vehicles as Middle East war sends petrol prices soaring 54%
Article Text:
Pakistan fuel prices to be revised every day

Poll Vote & Share your view How do rising oil prices influence your view on transitioning to electric vehicles? Strongly encourage me to switch Have no impact on my decision 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

EV sales accelerate amid fuel price pressure

Pakistan expects to achieve its electric-vehicle adoption target ahead of schedule as surging oil prices make the shift away from petrol-powered vehicles increasingly attractive, a senior government official said.The government aims for electric vehicles to account for 30% of new vehicle sales by 2030 under its EV policy announced last year. Haroon Akhtar, adviser to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on industries and production, said the sharp rise in fuel prices has reduced the time needed for buyers to recover the higher upfront cost of EVs.“I feel that the target we had set in our electric-vehicle policy last year, we will achieve it much earlier as rise in oil prices has brought cost recovery of EV to one to one and a half year,” Akhtar told Bloomberg in Islamabad.“People are realizing the benefit now. You don't have to pay for petrol,” he said.Petrol and diesel prices in Pakistan have risen 54% and 43%, respectively, since the Middle East conflict began in February, according to data available from Pakistan State Oil Company Ltd.Akhtar said sales of electric motorcycles and scooters have tripled from a year earlier, while electric-car sales have doubled, although industry-wide EV sales data is not publicly available.“This is an impact of the Middle East conflict, as fuel prices have gone up,” Akhtar said.Despite the growing incentive to switch to EVs, factors including high vehicle costs and limited charging infrastructure mean a large-scale transformation of Pakistan’s vehicle fleet and oil consumption will take years.The government is also preparing a new auto policy that could be presented to the cabinet within the next two weeks. It is considering tax incentives for EVs to narrow the price gap between electric and conventional vehicles, Akhtar said.
Article Summary: Pakistan aims for electric vehicles to account for 30% of new vehicle sales by 2030. The sharp rise in fuel prices has reduced the time needed for buyers to recover the higher upfront cost of EVs. The government is also preparing a new auto policy that could be presented to the cabinet within the next two weeks.

Article Title: Pakistan forces accused of quadcopter blast that killed 2 children in Balochistan
Article Text:
Pakistan forces accused of quadcopter link

A blast in Balochistan's Panjgur district killed two children and left three others injured, The Balochistan Post reported. The incident took place in Fateh Ali Bazaar in Gowargo tehsil, where the children had been playing.According to the report, the children noticed an unidentified object hanging from a tree. The object exploded after it was disturbed, killing two boys aged nine and 10. Three other boys, aged seven, nine and 12, were injured.The nature of the device that caused the explosion remains unclear.However, local sources alleged that it was connected to a quadcopter operated by Pakistani security forces. One source also claimed that explosives had been attached to a military quadcopter and placed in the area.The source further alleged that local journalists were later told to describe the incident as a hand-grenade blast or an explosion involving another device.The Panjgur incident comes amid other allegations of civilian casualties involving military drones and quadcopters in Balochistan.On September 24, four young men were killed and two others injured in an alleged military drone strike in Balicha, Kech, according to The Balochistan Post.Families of those killed said the men had gone there for a picnic and denied claims that they were militants.The incident triggered a boycott of courts across Makran, while lawyers called for an independent probe into the deaths.Earlier on September 18, five civilians were reportedly injured in alleged quadcopter attacks in Balochabad and Bullo in the Mand area, the report said.
Article Summary: Blast in Balochistan's Panjgur district killed two children and left three others injured. Local sources alleged that it was connected to a quadcopter operated by Pakistani security forces. Incident comes amid other allegations of civilian casualties involving military drones and quadcopters.

Article Title: Nearly 3 in 4 Pakistan inmates await trial amid prison overcrowding in country: Report
Article Text:
73% of Pakistan prisoners are under-trial, HRCP report finds

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the main cause of prison overcrowding in Pakistan? Delays in the justice system Arbitrary arrests Weak bail procedures Other reasons 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan's prisons are facing severe overcrowding, with people awaiting trial making up nearly three-fourths of the country's prison population, a Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) report has found.The report, 'Beyond the Prison Wall: Reducing Overcrowding in Pakistan's Prisons', said 73.41% of inmates were under-trial in 2024. The share has gone up from 66% in 2017, The Express Tribune reported.The report said Pakistan's prisons were operating at 152.2% of their approved capacity on average during July and August 2024.The HRCP said simply building more prisons would not address the problem. It pointed to delays in the justice system, including lengthy trials, weak bail procedures and the widespread use of pre-trial detention.Punjab faces an even bigger problem. According to official figures cited by the HRCP, 74,773 prisoners were held in 45 prisons across the province in September 2026. The sanctioned capacity was 39,204, meaning the prisons were operating at nearly 191% of capacity.Of the total inmates, 54,932 were awaiting trial.Punjab has added new prisons, barracks and other facilities over the years, but the report said the additional capacity has not matched the rise in the number of prisoners.The scale of the problem has grown majorly. Punjab province had 52,803 prisoners against a capacity of 21,527 in 2010. Overcrowding in the province stood at 173.6% in 2024, according to figures cited by The Express Tribune.The HRCP blamed arbitrary arrests, delays in investigations and lengthy prosecution for the growing number of people held without conviction.As a result, many accused people remain behind bars for months or even years while waiting for investigations and court proceedings to move forward, the report said.
Article Summary: 73.41% of inmates in Pakistan's prisons were under-trial in 2024. The share has gone up from 66% in 2017, according to a Human Rights Commission of Pakistan report. The HRCP said simply building more prisons would not address the problem. Delays in the justice system, arbitrary arrests and weak bail procedures were blamed.

Article Title: 'Come to your senses': What is Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif's condition for talks with Imran's party
Article Text:
Shehbaz’s talks offer fails to sway PTI as long march presses on

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think dialogue is the best way to resolve political disagreements? Yes, dialogue can help No, other steps are needed It depends on the situation 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Imran Khan-led Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Tuesday questioned the seriousness of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s offer for talks, calling it "merely symbolic" and saying the government had taken no concrete step beyond extending the invitation, Pakistan Today reported.PTI spokesperson Gohar said the Shehbaz Sharif-led government had also prevented PTI leaders from meeting the party’s founder and former PM Imran Khan , for nearly a year.Speaking to reporters in Rawalpindi, he said the last such meeting took place in October last year, Geo News reported.His remarks came after Sharif asked PTI to halt its ongoing long march towards Islamabad as a condition for holding talks.At an event in Islamabad, the prime minister warned that protests and long marches could hurt Pakistan’s economy. "I urge you to come to your senses, end the long march and sit-in, and then we will sit with you," he said.The PTI-led march, meanwhile, continued towards Peshawar on Monday, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi calling on party supporters to join the mobilisation.Afridi addressed march participants after the convoy reached Kohat and thanked residents for their "magnificent welcome". He said the convoy would resume its journey towards Peshawar from University Chowk on Tuesday, The Express Tribune reported.Declaring his loyalty to Imran Khan, Afridi said, “I am a soldier of Imran Khan. Even if the whole world comes together, it cannot put a price on me." He also urged supporters to send a message that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa belongs to Imran Khan.The chief minister had started the march from Lakki Marwat on Sunday after negotiations between PTI and the federal government failed to settle differences over the planned protest.Those talks, led by national assembly speaker Ayaz Sadiq, ended on Saturday without an agreement.The Pakistan government had asked PTI to call off the march, while the opposition sought assurances that its leaders would be permitted to meet long-imprisoned Imran Khan.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif asked PTI to halt its long march towards Islamabad as a condition for holding talks. PTI spokesperson said government had taken no concrete step beyond extending invitation. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi called on supporters to join mobilisation.

Article Title: Pakistan successfully test-fires extended version of Fatah-4 cruise missile
Article Text:
Senior Pakistan army officers, together with scientists and engineers, were reportedly present to watch the launch.

Pakistan successfully test-fired its homemade extended version of the ground-based Fatah-4 cruise missile on Tuesday.The cruise missile is capable of engaging long-range targets with high precision, the army said. PTI reported.In a statement, Pakistan Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said the “weapon system is capable of engaging targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality.”According to the Pakistan army, the test validated additional technical parameters of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability.Senior Pakistan army officers, together with scientists and engineers, were reportedly present to watch the launch.President Asif Ali Zardari , Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif , Field Marshal Asim Munir, who serves as Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, and the services chiefs praised the successful test.Pakistan had previously carried out a successful test of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile in May.The base version of Fatah-4 reportedly has a range of up to 750 kilometres and can reportedly hit targets with a five-metre accuracy.The military confirmed the new variant has an extended range but did not clarify how far.Fatah-4 is a conventional cruise missile of Islamabad’s army rocket force command. It flies at an altitude of about 50 meters to evade air defences and avoid radar detection.
